subject: Learning Methods
title: Why Teaching Deepens Understanding
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Why Teaching Deepens Understanding.

hook.text: Students who explained material to others scored 25 percent higher than those who only studied it themselves.

buildup.text: Explaining requires reorganizing knowledge into a coherent narrative. This reorganization creates deeper encoding.

discovery.text: The explanation effect says that the act of explaining forces you to fill gaps you didn't know you had.

twist.text: You don't need a real audience. Explaining to an empty chair or a rubber duck activates the same deep processing.

climax.text: After studying any topic, explain it aloud as if teaching a friend. Where you stumble is where you need to review.

punchline.text: Teach it to learn it. Stumbles reveal the gaps.

quiz.question: What makes explaining material to others so effective for learning?
options: It creates social pressure to memorize
Reorganizing knowledge for explanation forces you to fill gaps
Speaking activates a special memory region in the brain
